title_en: Xiang Meiqiong et al. v. Zhang Fengxia et al. — dispute over agency agreement for will execution
keywords_en: civil; dispute over agency agreement for execution of will; second instance; High People's Court; Shaanxi Province; natural person; legal person; Lawyers Law; General Principles of the Civil Law; validity of agency agreement for execution of will; determination of a lawyer representing both parties in the same case; legality of charging fees for execution of will; reversal; execution of will; agency agreement; lawyer's fees; inheritance; will; dispute over agency agreement for execution of will involving multiple persons
full_text_en:
Xiang Meiqiong et al. v. Zhang Fengxia et al. — Dispute over Agency Agreement for Execution of Will

[Ruling Summary]

Where a will executor enters into a voluntary agency agreement with the heirs regarding matters related to the execution of the will and collects fees for such execution in accordance with the agreement, in the absence of the testator having expressly provided for the executor's remuneration, such conduct does not fall within the prohibition under Article 34 of the Lawyers Law against a lawyer acting as agent for both parties in the same case. The agency agreement shall be deemed valid.

Plaintiffs: Xiang Meiqiong, female, 64 years old, residing at Gongbei New District, Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province.

Plaintiff: Xiong Weihao, male, 42 years old, residing at Pinghe District, Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province.

Plaintiff: Xiong Ping, female, 35 years old, residing at Pingsha District, Zhuhai City, Guangdong Province.

Defendants: Zhang Fengxia, female, 55 years old, lawyer of Shaanxi Jinbao Law Firm, residing at Baoji County, Shaanxi Province.

Defendants: Zhang Xu, male, 58 years old, lawyer of Shaanxi Jinbao Law Firm, residing at Baoji County, Shaanxi Province.

Defendants: Zhang Linlu, male, 54 years old, lawyer of Shaanxi Jinbao Law Firm, residing at Baoji County, Shaanxi Province.

Defendants: Feng Shuyi, male, 48 years old, employee of Shaanxi Baoji Brewery, residing at Baoji County, Shaanxi Province.

Plaintiffs Xiang Meiqiong, Xiong Weihao, and Xiong Ping filed an action with the Baoji Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province against Defendants Zhang Fengxia, Zhang Xu, Zhang Linlu, and Feng Shuyi concerning a dispute over an agency agreement for the execution of a will.

The plaintiffs, Xiang Meiqiong, Xiong Weihao, and Xiong Ping, alleged: We are the heirs of Xiong Yiwu. In his will, Xiong Yiwu designated the defendant Zhang Fengxia as the executor of the will. After Xiong Yiwu's death, Zhang Fengxia failed to actively distribute the estate to the heirs in accordance with the testator's instructions. Instead, she misled us into signing an agency agreement for the execution of the will and deducted so-called agency fees for will execution in the amount of RMB 229,000, thereby infringing upon our lawful property rights and interests. We request the revocation or declaration of invalidity of the two agency agreements for will execution, an order for Zhang Fengxia to return the agency fee of RMB 229,000, and that the partners of the law firm where Zhang Fengxia originally worked bear joint and several liability.

Defendant Zhang Fengxia argued: The agreements I signed with Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping reflect the true intent of both parties. As the will executor designated by Xiong Yiwu during his lifetime, entering into an agency agreement with the heirs to further define the specific matters of will execution is lawful and valid. Charging the plaintiffs fees for the execution and inheritance of the estate complies with the provisions on lawyer fee collection. The agreement signed with plaintiffs Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping and Xiong Yiwu's designation of me as will executor are two separate legal relationships. I have committed no fault in the legal agency services and should not be required to return the agency fees.

Defendant Zhang Xu argued: Lawyer Zhang Fengxia, entrusted by the law firm, signed the agency agreement for will execution with the plaintiffs and negotiated the collection of agency fees. This constitutes a lawyer's professional conduct and is reasonable and lawful. The plaintiffs' request that all partners of the cooperative law firm bear joint and several liability for the return of the agency fees lacks legal basis.

Defendants Zhang Linlu and Feng Shuyi did not file a defense and, despite being summoned by the court, did not appear to respond to the action.

The Baoji Intermediate People's Court found the following facts upon trial:

On February 23, 1997, Xiong Yiwu, husband of plaintiff Xiang Meiqiong and father of Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping, requested defendant Zhang Fengxia, who was then a lawyer at Zhengda Law Firm, to witness and draft a will. The will distributed his assets, including cash, enterprises, and real estate, among the statutory heirs and others. He also engaged Zhang Fengxia as his lifelong legal counsel and designated Zhang Fengxia as the executor of the will. Seven copies of the will were made, all kept by Zhang Fengxia, to be implemented by Zhang Fengxia upon the commencement of inheritance. On February 28, 1997, Xiong Yiwu passed away. On March 1 and April 14, 1997, Zhang Fengxia signed agreements with Xiong Ping and Xiong Weihao, respectively. Based on Xiong Yiwu's will, the agreements mainly provided for the following: Zhang Fengxia shall complete all procedures in accordance with the provisions of the will; Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping engaged Zhang Fengxia as legal counsel and financial advisor to protect their lawful rights and interests, and fully authorized Zhang Fengxia to audit the inherited enterprise property to ensure the full realization of the rights and interests of Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping; the lawyer's fee for property division agency in the execution of the will shall be deducted from the estate in accordance with state regulations. Since Xiang Meiqiong was mentally ill, her civil actions were represented by Xiong Weihao. On April 22, 1997, Zhang Fengxia issued receipts to Xiang Meiqiong and Xiong Weihao, respectively, for the collection of RMB 150,000 and RMB 30,000 as lawyer fees for will property division agency by Zhengda Law Firm. However, the collected RMB 180,000 was not turned over to Zhengda Law Firm. On April 7, 1997, Zhang Fengxia issued a "Statement of Explanation" to Xiong Ping, stating that all fees for the execution of the will had been settled. At trial, Zhang Fengxia admitted to actually receiving RMB 20,000 in cash from Xiong Ping, for which no receipt was issued. By the end of April 1997, Zhang Fengxia had fully distributed the estate in accordance with Xiong Yiwu's will. During the period of will execution from March to April 1997, Zhang Fengxia received total wages, subsidies, and consulting fees of RMB 3,048 from the Northern Group Company, and had her travel expenses reimbursed.

It was further found that Zhengda Law Firm was a cooperative law firm established on July 25, 1994, upon approval by the Shaanxi Provincial Department of Justice, and was formed by four applicants: Zhang Xu, Zhang Linlu, Zhang Fengxia, and Feng Shuyi. On January 1, 1998, Zhang Xu and Zhang Linlu withdrew from Zhengda Law Firm. On March 24, 1998, after liquidation, Zhengda Law Firm was transferred to the Baoji County Bureau of Justice.

The above facts are confirmed by the following primary evidence:
1. Statements of the parties at trial.
2. The will of Xiong Yiwu during his lifetime and its notarization.
3. The two agreements signed by Zhang Fengxia with Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping, respectively.
4. Two payment receipts from Zhengda Law Firm issued by Zhang Fengxia to Xiang Meiqiong and Xiong Weihao.
5. "Property Execution Transfer Form" for Xiong Yiwu's estate.
6. "Statement of Explanation" issued by Zhang Fengxia to Xiong Ping.
7. The transfer document from Zhengda Law Firm to the Baoji County Bureau of Justice.

The Baoji Intermediate People's Court held:

Article 34 of the Lawyers Law provides: "A lawyer shall not act as an agent for both parties in the same case." Paragraph 1, Item (5) of Article 58 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of the Civil Law) stipulates that "a civil act that violates the law or the public interest is void." Article 61 provides: "If a civil act is confirmed to be void or is revoked, the property acquired by the party as a result of such act shall be returned to the party who suffered the loss. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for the damages incurred thereby; if both parties are at fault, each shall bear its own corresponding liability." The agency contracts entered into by defendant Zhang Fengxia with plaintiffs Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping in the form of agreements had their substantive content derived from the will of Xiong Yiwu during his lifetime. Zhang Fengxia, as a lawyer, accepted Xiong Yiwu's lifetime entrustment to serve as his estate executor. This should be regarded as the formation of an agency relationship by mandate with Xiong Yiwu during his lifetime. When executing the will, Zhang Fengxia deducted agency fees from the estate. This not only violated the testator's lifetime entrustment and caused loss to the heirs' property but also contravened the prohibitive provisions of the Lawyers Law. Therefore, the plaintiffs' request to declare the agency agreement for will execution invalid should be supported. Zhang Fengxia, as a practicing lawyer, should have known the provisions of Chinese law on lawyers' professional conduct. However, when signing the contracts with the plaintiffs, she failed to act in accordance with the law, committing negligence in contracting. She shall bear full liability for the invalidity of the contracts. The RMB 200,000 obtained through the invalid contracts shall be returned. Plaintiff Xiong Ping claimed the return of RMB 49,000, but Zhang Fengxia admitted to collecting only RMB 20,000. Since Xiong Ping could not provide evidence to support her claim, the claim regarding Zhang Fengxia's collection of RMB 49,000 in agency fees is not upheld. Upon liquidation on March 24, 1998, Zhengda Law Firm should be deemed to have been legally dissolved. Given that its fee collection had always been through unified receipts issued by the firm with individual collection by lawyers, and since Zhang Fengxia was the actual holder of the property in dispute, the civil liability for returning the agency fees shall be borne by Zhang Fengxia. The plaintiffs' request that all partners of Zhengda Law Firm bear joint and several liability is not supported.

Accordingly, on October 26, 2000, the Baoji Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment:
1. The agreements for will execution signed by defendant Zhang Fengxia with Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping are void;
2. Defendant Zhang Fengxia shall return RMB 30,000 to plaintiff Xiang Meiqiong, RMB 150,000 to plaintiff Xiong Weihao, and RMB 20,000 to plaintiff Xiong Ping;
3. All other claims of plaintiffs Xiang Meiqiong, Xiong Weihao, and Xiong Ping are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, Zhang Fengxia, dissatisfied, appealed to the Shaanxi High People's Court.

Zhang Fengxia's grounds of appeal were: My signing of the agency agreements for will execution with Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping in my capacity as Xiong Yiwu's will executor does not constitute "acting as an agent for both parties in the same case." I request confirmation that the agreements signed by Zhengda Law Firm with Xiong Ping and Xiong Weihao, respectively, are lawful and valid.

Based on the evidence adduced at first instance, the Shaanxi High People's Court found the following:

Xiang Meiqiong's husband and Xiong Weihao and Xiong Ping's father, Xiong Yiwu, was involved in a car accident in Xun County, Henan Province, on October 17, 1996. Subsequently, due to his severe illness, he was transferred to Xi'an Honghui Hospital in Shaanxi Province for treatment.

On February 23, 1997, Xiong Yiwu invited Zhang Fengxia to Xi'an and, with Sun Yapeng (Xiong Yiwu's secretary), Xiong Weihao, and Wu Qiuwen (Xiong Ping's husband) present at his bedside, had Zhang Fengxia draft his will. The content was as follows: "I unfortunately suffered a car accident while inspecting work in Xun County, Henan Province, on October 17, 1996. I am currently hospitalized in the recovery phase. To express gratitude for Zhang Jinyun's care and to fulfill my wishes, I write this will. 1. Cash: The existing cash of RMB 13,160,396.73 (temporarily in the custody of Wu Qiuwen and Zhang Jinyun) shall be divided into four shares: one share each for Xiong Weihao, Xiong Ping, Zhang Jinyun, and Xiang Meiqiong. Xiang Meiqiong's share shall be kept by Xiong Weihao and used jointly by Xiang Meiqiong and Xiong Hong. 2. Enterprises: (1) Shares in Yantai Yiwu Food Co., Ltd. shall be inherited by son Xiong Weihao and daughter Xiong Ping, with son-in-law Wu Qiuwen participating in management on their behalf; any profits realized shall belong to them jointly. (2) Mehekou Xiong Yiwu Food Co., Ltd. shall be managed by Comrade Zhang Jinyun on my behalf, in accordance with the original contract. Because my success in my career today is due to my wife Zhang Jinyun's care, concern, and support, any profits realized shall belong to Comrade Zhang Jinyun. (3) Baoji Yiwu Food Co., Ltd. and Xiong Yiwu Northern Group Xingping Company shall be managed by Xiong Weihao, assisted by Attorney Zhang Fengxia; any profits realized shall belong to Xiong Weihao. 3. Real Estate: (1) The house located in Pingsha, Zhuhai City, belongs to Xiong Weihao. (2) The properties in Guangzhou and the shops in Panyu belong to Xiong Ping. (3) The properties in Lifeng New Village, Mehekou City, and in Fuxin, as well as the storefront properties in Fuxin City Center, belong to Zhang Jinyun. 4. Others: (1) I retain Attorney Zhang Fengxia of Baoji County Zhengda Law Firm as my personal lifetime legal counsel, with the authority to review the accounts of the aforesaid enterprises and protect my lawful rights and interests. (2) I designate Attorney Zhang Fengxia as the executor of my will. (3) Currently, due to difficulty in writing, the will is written by legal counsel Zhang Fengxia. (4) After the expiration of the contracts I have signed with various companies, if the trademarks continue to be used, 20% of the profits shall be extracted as trademark usage fees (separate contracts to be signed); the enterprise to which the trademark belongs shall enjoy the benefits. (5) This will is made in seven copies, to be kept by the will executor. Upon the commencement of inheritance, the executor shall be responsible for implementation. Witnesses: Zhang Fengxia (signature), Unit: Baoji County Zhengda Law Firm; Witness: Sun Yapeng (signature), Unit: Xiong Yiwu Group Company; Witnessing relative: Xiong Weihao (signature); Wu Qiuwen (signature); Testator: Xiong Yiwu; Drafter: Zhang Fengxia; Date of will: February 23, 1997." This will was notarized by the Baoji City Notary Public Office.

Xiong Yiwu died on February 28, 1997. On March 1 and April 14, 1997, Zhang Fengxia signed "Agreements" with Xiong Ping and Xiong Weihao, respectively, stipulating: In accordance with items (1), (2), and (4) of Section Four of the will of Mr. Xiong Yiwu dated February 23, 1997, the parties have negotiated and signed the following agreement: 1. Party B (Zhang Fengxia) shall complete all procedures in accordance with the provisions of the will; travel expenses shall be borne by Party A (Xiong Ping, Xiong Weihao). 2. Party A engages Party B as legal counsel and financial advisor to protect the lawful rights and interests of Party B, and fully authorizes Party B to ensure the full realization of Party A's inherited rights and interests. Audit shall be conducted in accordance with the president's instructions. 3. During the performance of this contract, Party B shall assist in resolving any legal or financial issues encountered by Party A. 4. Remuneration for Party B: To be implemented in accordance with the original legal counsel contract, paid by the Group office. Bonuses shall be determined at Party A's discretion. 5. Regardless of whether Party A holds a position in this entity, Party B has the right to act on behalf of Party A in accordance with this agreement. 6. The lawyer's fee for will property division agency shall be deducted from the estate in accordance with state regulations. 7. This agreement is valid for three years, commencing from the date of signing." On April 22, 1997, Zhang Fengxia issued payment receipts to Xiong Weihao and Xiang Meiqiong for RMB 150,000 and RMB 30,000 as lawyer fees for will property division agency by Baoji County Zhengda Law Firm. However, the collected RMB 180,000 was not turned over to Zhengda Law Firm. On April 7, 1997, in a "Statement of Explanation" to Xiong Ping, Zhang Fengxia stated that all fees for the execution of the will had been settled. At trial, Zhang Fengxia stated that she had personally collected the RMB 20,000 in cash and had not issued a receipt to Xiong Ping. This totaled RMB 200,000. By the end of April 1997, Zhang Fengxia had fully distributed Xiong Yiwu's estate in accordance with his will.

On June 13, 1997, plaintiffs Xiang Meiqiong, Xiong Weihao, and Xiong Ping filed an action with the Baoji Intermediate People's Court, alleging that Zhang Fengxia, in her capacity as will executor, distributed RMB 3.29 million of Xiong Yiwu's assets to Zhang Jinyun, who was claimed to be Xiong Yiwu's "wife," as an unlawful acquisition. They requested a declaration that the "Will" was void; an order for Zhang Jinyun to return the unlawfully obtained RMB 3.29 million; and an order for Zhang Fengxia to refund the execution fee of RMB 229,000. The Baoji Intermediate People's Court accepted the case on August 15, 1997, and issued notices to respond to Zhang Jinyun and Zhang Fengxia. Zhang Jinyun raised an objection to jurisdiction, arguing that the case should not be heard by the Baoji Intermediate People's Court, but her objection was dismissed by the Baoji Intermediate People's Court. Zhang Jinyun, dissatisfied, appealed to the Shaanxi High People's Court. The Shaanxi High People's Court held: The plaintiffs' request for a declaration of invalidity of Xiong Yiwu's "Will" neither constitutes a dispute over the return of property nor a tort dispute but is an inheritance dispute. The dispute between the plaintiffs and Zhang Fengxia is not a dispute over the return of property but a dispute over agency fees. Therefore, it ruled that the inheritance dispute be transferred to the Jilin High People's Court, the court of the situs of the immovable property, for handling (that case has now been concluded); the dispute over agency fees between the plaintiffs and Zhang Fengxia shall have its jurisdiction determined by the Baoji Intermediate People's Court. The present action is the one re-filed after the plaintiffs amended their claims.

During the second instance, with the Shaanxi High People's Court presiding over mediation, Xiong Ping voluntarily waived her claims against appellant Zhang Fengxia and reached a mediation agreement with Zhang Fengxia regarding the acceptance fees for the first and second instances. The mediation agreement was signed by both parties and has taken legal effect.

The Shaanxi High People's Court held that the issue in dispute between the parties in this case is: Is the agency agreement entered into by Zhang Fengxia, as the will executor, with some of the heirs concerning matters related to the execution of the will valid?

Neither the General Principles of the Civil Law nor the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China clearly stipulates the legal status of a will executor or the rights and obligations of a will executor. Provided that the prohibitive provisions of the law are not violated, civil subjects have the right to dispose of their own rights. Zhang Fengxia, as the will executor designated by Xiong Yiwu, in the absence of Xiong Yiwu having clearly provided for remuneration for executing the will, entered into agreements with heirs Xiong Weihao, Xiong Ping, and others concerning matters related to the execution of the will, and collected fees for will execution in accordance with such agreements. This does not fall within the prohibition under Article 34 of the Lawyers Law against a lawyer acting as an agent for both parties in the same case. The first-instance judgment's determination that the agreements between the parties were void by applying Article 34 of the Lawyers Law constitutes an error in the application of law and should be corrected.

Whether the agency agreements entered into between Xiong Weihao and others and Zhang Fengxia are valid should be examined in accordance with the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. Although Xiong Weihao and others alleged that they signed the agency agreements with Zhang Fengxia under Zhang Fengxia's misleading influence, they failed to provide corresponding evidence to prove that the agreements were signed against their true intent, or that the agreements were void or voidable contracts as provided by law. Therefore, their request to revoke or declare the two agency agreements void is not supported by law.

In conclusion, in accordance with Paragraph 1, Item (2) of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment on March 1, 2003, is as follows:

1. The civil judgment of the Baoji Intermediate People's Court is reversed;
2. The agreement for will execution signed by Zhang Fengxia of Baoji County Zhengda Law Firm with Xiong Weihao is valid;
3. The claims of Xiang Meiqiong and Xiong Weihao are dismissed.

This judgment is final.
